To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HTL is a modular system that can be assembled from its subunits, that the HTL can be produced in a balanced stoichiometric manner, that it is functional, and that it is capable of interacting with RNC complexes to form RNC-HTL complexes.

we developed a modular approach for balanced expression of the SecYEG, SecDF, and YidC subunits of the holotranslocomplex (HTL), which is a multiprotein complex that is essential for translocation of nascent polypeptides across the cytoplasmic membrane in bacteria.

we have developed an efficient and robust protocol for the production and purification of the prokaryote-specific multiprotein complex, the Sec-dependent protein secretion and insertion system, the SecY-SecE-SecG (YEG)-SecDF-SecYajC (DFYajC)-YidC holotranlocon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and construction of recombinant DNA constructs for the expression of the HTL and its RNC supercomplex in E. coli, and the subsequent purification of the recombinant complexes.
a novel, generalizable, and modular approach for balanced, coexpression of recombinants of multiprotein complexes in Escherichia coli.
the molecular mechanisms of protein secretion and insertion into membranes in the bacterial cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this protocol provides a general strategy for the production of recombinant protein complexes in E. coli.

the ACEMBL approach for balanced overproduction of multiprotein complexes in the E. coli expression system, with the SecYEG-HTL complex used as an example, is a robust, versatile, modular and reproducible procedure that is applicable to the overexpression of a wide range of recombinant proteins and protein complexes.

the modular approach described here can be successfully applied to the overexpression and purification of recombinant protein complexes in E. colia and that the HTL is an excellent example of this approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to reconstitute in E. coli a functional prokaryotic secretory and insertion machinery, the holotranslocons (HTL), which has been used to study the mechanism of protein translocation.
the SecYEG-YidC-HTL system is an excellent example to illustrate the potential and the limitations of the ACEMBL approach for the production of functional multiprotein complexes.
this procedure can be used to study protein translocation and insertion in vitro, and it may be applied for the production of other multiprotein complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

balanced overexpression of multiprotein complexes in bacteria can be accomplished by a modular design of DNA constructs and by the use of a suitable vector system, which is compatible with high-level expression and purification of the target proteins.

the design and implementation of a multiprotein complex overexpression system is not only a technical challenge but also a conceptual one, requiring the consideration of the stoichiometry and functional interactions between the subcomplexes and the subunits of the target complex.
the ACEMBL approach is applicable to the overexpression of any other multiprotein complexes in the cell.
